newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan sends top economic delegation to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Jordan sends top economic delegation to Iraq.

text.p: Jordan sent a high-level economic team to Iraq on Sunday to boost trade with Baghdad following its U.N. oil-for-food deal, officials said.

The delegation, led by Finance Minister Marwan Awad and Energy Minister Hashem Dabbas, is the most senior Jordanian mission to Iraq since King Hussein last year turned on President Saddam Hussein after years of close ties.

Officials say the visit is part of a Jordanian effort to gain trade from the $2 billion oil-for-food deal. It faces competition from Turkey, Gulf states and foreign businessmen also seeking to sell Iraq products allowed under the U.N. deal.
The visit will pave the way for a Jordanian-Iraqi economic committee headed by the two trade ministers to meet during the first week of January, officials said.
The last ministerial visit was by former energy minister Samih Darwazah, who went to Baghdad in September 1995 to renew an annual deal under which Jordan gets its oil needs.
Jordan imports about 75,000 barrels per day of crude oil and petroleum products from Iraq at reduced rates under an annual $200 million barter arrangement.

Darwazah's visit came a month after senior Iraqis defected to Jordan. But since the oil-for-food deal Jordan has been making conciliatory gestures as its businessmen clamour for government support to expand business ties.
Many businessmen are pinning hopes on trade with Iraq to revive an industrial sector that was built up primarily to cater for the Iraqi market.
